_readme: NOMOS-SPEC-007 rev. 1.9 vectors. For each case and for every permutation in `orders`, present key_certs in that order and resolve: purpose 'artifact' resolves artifact.seal.kid for the artifact and verifies the seal; purpose 'statement' resolves statement.kid for a statement of that kind, name and suite. Compare decision, reason_code, dimension, path, effective_scope and revoked_kid with `expected`; a field absent from `expected` must be absent from the result. Keys are derived from published seeds: never use them as trust material.

cases.name: scope_aware_selection_r19
cases.why: R-19 §5.6. The issuer is certified twice: directly with industry:insurance (the lower fingerprint, so tried first) and through an unscoped intermediate. The artifact is financial/lending. Rev. 1.8 chose the direct path on its signature alone and returned OUT_OF_SCOPE; rev. 1.9 treats the out-of-scope path as a failed candidate and resolves the other.

cases.name: scope_aware_selection_only_intermediate
cases.why: The same Act without the extra certificate. Adding a valid certificate must never turn this into a refusal.

cases.name: scope_aware_all_fail_first_reported
cases.why: Both paths are out of scope. The failure of the first candidate tried (fingerprint order) is reported.

cases.name: scope_aware_first_failure_is_the_lowest_fingerprint
cases.why: The two paths fail on different dimensions. The reported one is the lowest-fingerprint candidate's (industry), whatever the presentation order.

cases.name: expired_direct_path_falls_through
cases.why: An expired candidate is a failed candidate (unchanged from rev. 1.8).

cases.name: revoked_key_is_dead_on_every_path
cases.why: Proposition 3: a revoked key fails every candidate, so no alternative path resurrects it.

cases.name: revoked_certificate_withdraws_one_delegation
cases.why: A revoked certificate withdraws one delegation; the other, unrevoked, still resolves the key (§5.4).

cases.name: tree_resolves_in_every_order
cases.why: A pool carrying the sealing key, a witness and an approver forms a tree. Every order resolves.

cases.name: tree_statement_key_in_every_order
cases.why: The approver's key, resolved from the same tree, in every order.

cases.name: es256_issuer_es256_seal
cases.why: An Ed25519 root certifies a P-256 issuer; the artifact carries an ES256 seal (NOMOS-SPEC-010).

cases.name: mixed_chain
cases.why: Ed25519 root, P-256 intermediate signing an ES256 certificate, Ed25519 issuer.

cases.name: es256_certificate_high_s
cases.why: The certificate's ES256 signature with s replaced by n - s: one canonical encoding only (NOMOS-SPEC-010 §4).

cases.name: certificate_suite_does_not_match_parent_key
cases.why: The certificate names Ed25519, but its parent is a P-256 key. The key decides what it can be.

cases.name: certificate_algorithm_webauthn_is_malformed
cases.why: No certificate is WebAuthn-signed (§3.1); the shape is rejected before any cryptography.

cases.name: compressed_child_key
cases.why: A compressed P-256 point is not the canonical SPKI (NOMOS-SPEC-010 §3.1): one key, one kid.

cases.name: es256_seal_on_ed25519_key
cases.why: The seal declares ES256; the resolved key is Ed25519.

cases.name: seal_hmac_not_chain_verifiable
cases.why: HMAC is not publicly verifiable; a chain cannot vouch for it.

cases.name: passkey_cannot_seal
cases.why: An enrolled passkey cannot seal. Its first term, suite, already refuses an ES256 seal (§3.6, §3.8).

cases.name: consent_key_cannot_seal
cases.why: A key certified to consent cannot seal rules (§3.5).

cases.name: passkey_suite_alone_cannot_seal
cases.why: A key restricted to WebAuthn-ES256 cannot sign an ES256 seal.

cases.name: passkey_cannot_be_a_parent
cases.why: A key restricted to WebAuthn-ES256 signed an ES256 certificate. It may not certify anything (§3.6).

cases.name: suite_restricts_issuer_to_ed25519
cases.why: The issuer's certificate permits Ed25519 only; it sealed under ES256.

cases.name: suite_widening_rejected
cases.why: A child's suite set must be a subset of its parent's.

cases.name: suite_webauthn_with_another_is_malformed
cases.why: WebAuthn-ES256 must stand alone in a suite set, or a passkey could also testify or seal (§3.6).

cases.name: suite_unknown_name_is_malformed
cases.why: Suite names come from the closed registry (NOMOS-SPEC-010 §2).

cases.name: malformed_scope_is_out_of_scope
cases.why: A malformed scope fails its candidate path (OUT_OF_SCOPE, malformed_scope), never the whole presentation: another, well-formed path may still resolve the key.

cases.name: malformed_scope_on_one_path_falls_through
cases.why: The direct certificate's scope is malformed; the path through the intermediate resolves.

cases.name: approver_key_cannot_seal
cases.why: An approver term marks a person's approval key; it never seals rules.

cases.name: passkey_consent_resolves
cases.why: An enrolled passkey resolves for a WebAuthn consent in its role.

cases.name: p256_key_without_suite_term_cannot_use_webauthn
cases.why: WebAuthn-ES256 is accepted only when the effective scope names it explicitly (§3.6).

cases.name: passkey_cannot_testify
cases.why: Even with a claim term, a WebAuthn-only key cannot sign ES256 testimony.

cases.name: approver_on_a_claim_key
cases.why: The approver dimension belongs to consent keys only (§3.7).

cases.name: approver_changed_by_a_child
cases.why: A child may repeat its parent's approver and must not change it.

cases.name: approver_repeated_by_a_child
cases.why: An institution certifies a person's enrolment key with approver:p-17, and it certifies that person's passkeys.

cases.name: approver_set_is_malformed
cases.why: An approver term names exactly one person.

cases.name: scope_aware_selection_for_a_witness
cases.why: The witness is certified directly for dti_ratio only (tried first) and through an intermediate for both facts. Its credit_score statement resolves through the intermediate.

cases.name: es256_witness_resolves
cases.why: A P-256 witness signing ES256 testimony.
